pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP) THE SMOKING GUN: Clear urine oxidizing into a dark port-wine color upon exposure to light, precipitated by caloric restriction in a patient with neurovisceral symptoms (severe abdominal pain, hyponatremia, motor neuropathy, and psychosis). PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Acute Intermittent Porphyria is an autosomal dominant metabolic disorder caused by a defect in porphobilinogen deaminase (PBGD), a crucial enzyme in the heme biosynthesis pathway. Caloric deprivation downregulates intracellular glucose, which induces hepatic ALAS1 enzyme activity. This leads to a massive accumulation of the neurotoxic heme precursors delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG). These toxic intermediates induce sympathetic hyperactivation, autonomic damage (causing neuropathic abdominal pain and hypertension), central nervous system dysfunction (psychosis and SIADH-induced hyponatremia), and motor axonal degeneration (causing ascending paralysis). When excess urinary porphobilinogen is exposed to air and light, it auto-oxidizes into porphobilin, turning the urine a classic port-wine shade.
